setup:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
rng = np.random.default_rng(99)
n = 1000
k = rng.integers(0, 3, n)
centers = rng.normal(0, 8, (3, 10))
df = pd.DataFrame(centers[k] + rng.normal(0, 1, (n, 10)), columns=[f'x{i}' for i in range(10)])
m = 60
k2 = rng.integers(0, 2, m)
df2 = pd.DataFrame(centers[k2] + rng.normal(0, 1, (m, 10)), columns=[f'x{i}' for i in range(10)])
df2['label'] = ['alpha' if v == 0 else 'beta' for v in k2]

steps.name: wait for overlay XY and describe
steps.until: (() => { const ov = a.layers.find(l => l.kind === 'point-overlay'); return ov && (a.overlayFilled.get(ov.id) ?? 0) >= (a.overlayNKept.get(ov.id) ?? 1) && a.overlayDescribes.has(ov.id); })()

steps.name: verify overlay describe contains label column
assert: (() => { const ov = a.layers.find(l => l.kind === 'point-overlay'); const cols = a.overlayDescribes.get(ov.id); return cols && cols.some(c => c.name === 'label'); })()
steps.report: (() => { const ov = a.layers.find(l => l.kind === 'point-overlay'); return { cols: a.overlayDescribes.get(ov.id)?.map(c => c.name) }; })()

steps.name: search overlay for alpha
steps.eval: const ov = a.layers.find(l => l.kind === 'point-overlay'); const cols = a.overlayDescribes.get(ov.id); const labelCol = cols.find(c => c.name === 'label'); a.runSearchOverlay(ov.id, labelCol.index, 'alpha')

steps.name: verify overlay search results
steps.report: { searchMatchCount: a.searchMatchCount, searchQuery: a.searchQuery, searchLayerId: a.searchLayerId }
